# Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Vin02a2)

**ID:** Atk Vin02a2
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Vinayapiṭake (Dutiyo bhāgo) (atk-vin02)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Vinaya

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā* constitutes the commentary on the *Mahāvagga* of the *Vinayapiṭaka*, cataloged in the Burmese Chaṭṭhasaṅgāyana collection as the second volume of the Vinaya commentary (*Aṭṭhakathā Vinayapiṭake (Dutiyo bhāgo)*) within the *Samantapāsādikā* [Galasek 2016; Nyanatusita 2008]. It provides legal definitions, background narratives, and word-by-word commentary on the khandhaka rules, covering sections such as the *Mahākhandhaka* and episodes like the *Coravatthukathā* [Galasek 2016]. For example, in explaining monastic regulations on eligibility for the *pabbajjā* ordination, it glosses the term *dhajabandha* to clarify the prohibition against ordaining notorious bandits who are openly recognized for committing crimes such as village plunder or highway robbery [Galasek 2016]. Later Pali exegetical traditions also produced subcommentarial aids on this portion, including the *Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā-yojanā* [Nyanatusita 2008].

DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse between the *Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā* and 206 other Pali texts across 20,135 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial overlaps occur with Vinaya subcommentaries and compendia, notably the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* (1,311 matches, including a passage covering §836_0–860_0 aligned with §764_0–776_0), the *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* (1,307 matches), the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* (767 matches), the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* (813 matches), and the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* (916 matches) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares 575 segments with its canonical root text, the *Mahākhandhaka*, alongside cross-commentarial reuse with the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with a score of 10 or higher are recorded by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
